sample_llm_prompt.description: Structured prompt sent to LLM for feedback generation

example.system_role: You are a certified yoga instructor providing friendly, encouraging feedback.
example.user_prompt:
Pose Detected: warrior2
Confidence: 89.3%
User Level: beginner

Current Body Angles:
- Left Knee: 95° (ideal: 90°, diff: 5°)
- Right Knee: 178° (ideal: 180°, diff: 2°)
- Left Hip: 88° (ideal: 90°, diff: 2°)
- Torso Vertical: 8° (ideal: 0°, diff: 8°)

Issues Detected:
- front knee slightly forward
- torso slight lean

Provide 2-3 specific, actionable corrections in friendly language. Be encouraging and supportive. Keep response under 60 words. Focus on the most important corrections first.

examples.feedback: Nice effort! Your front knee is tracking a bit forward (95°). Try shifting your hips back slightly so your knee stays directly over your ankle. This protects your knee joint.
Good start! I notice your spine is slightly rounded (25° curve). Try bending your knees a bit and lifting your tailbone higher. Focus on lengthening your spine rather than straightening your legs.
Excellent Tree Pose! Your standing leg is strong and straight at 180°. Your balance is impressive. Keep your gaze steady on one point and hold for 5 more breaths!
Strong plank! Your hips are dipping about 15° below neutral. Engage your core and imagine a straight line from head to heels. Think about lifting your belly button toward your spine.
Beautiful extension! Your torso is rotated about 30° forward. Try opening your chest more toward the ceiling by stacking your shoulders. Imagine your body between two panes of glass.

ideal_angles_reference.description: Reference angles for common yoga poses

warrior2.description: Front knee at 90° over ankle, back leg straight, torso upright, arms extended

warrior1.description: Similar to Warrior 2 but hips square forward

downdog.description: Inverted V-shape, straight arms and legs, neutral spine

tree.description: Standing leg straight, bent leg at 90°, torso upright

plank.description: Straight line from head to heels, arms extended

triangle.description: Both legs straight, torso parallel to ground, arms in line

chair.description: Knees bent at 90°, sitting back, slight forward lean

cobra.description: Gentle backbend, elbows slightly bent, chest lifted

bridge.description: Knees at 90°, hips lifted to create straight line from knees to shoulders

child.description: Resting pose, hips on heels, forehead on mat, arms extended

common_issues_reference.description: Common posture issues and their corrections

front_knee_too_bent.correction: Raise your hips slightly to achieve a 90° angle

front_knee_not_bent_enough.correction: Bend your front knee deeper until it's directly over your ankle

knee_forward_of_ankle.correction: Shift your hips back to protect your knee joint

back_knee_bent.correction: Straighten your back leg and press through your heel

rounded_back.correction: Lengthen through your back and lift your chest

torso_leaning.correction: Engage your core and stack your shoulders over your hips

hips_sagging.correction: Engage your core and lift your belly button toward your spine

elbows_bent.correction: Straighten your arms and press firmly through your hands

shoulders_raised.correction: Relax your shoulders down away from your ears

uneven_hips.correction: Level your pelvis by adjusting your stance or using a prop
